hypotheses.justification: Completeness can be dropped because the right-hand side already requires the constant coefficient to be a unit. The formal power series then has an inverse. For each k, the restriction condition makes f modulo I^k a polynomial; its nonconstant coefficients are nilpotent modulo I^k, and there are only finitely many of them. Thus its nonconstant part is nilpotent, so this polynomial is a unit and its polynomial inverse agrees with the reduction of the formal inverse. That shows the inverse is adically restricted. Conversely, a restricted unit reduces modulo I to a unit polynomial, whose nonconstant coefficients are nilpotent, giving the stated radical condition; its constant coefficient is a unit. These arguments do not require IsAdicComplete.
